instruction: Type the title '深圳福田区地址列表' at the top of the open Word document and save it.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter');

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened Chrome, attempted to search for 24-hour self-service visa check-in machine addresses in Futian District via Google (SSL error), sz.gov.cn, Baidu (irrelevant results for '24'), and visaforchina.cn (blocked by captcha). Never found the addresses and never wrote anything in the Word document. Hit 50-turn limit.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome and navigate to URLs, type in address bars and search bars, switch between browser tabs, interact with Chinese government websites (sz.gov.cn), navigate to Baidu. Can interact with LibreOffice Writer window (visible in initial screenshot).
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed because: (1) Google had SSL certificate error (NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID), (2) could not formulate effective search queries on government site or Baidu to find specific visa machine locations, (3) visaforchina.cn blocked with captcha verification, (4) never returned to Writer to type any content. Spent all 50 turns trying different web searches without success.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original complex web-search-then-write task into a simple direct typing task in Writer. No web search required - tests basic Writer interaction within model's demonstrated capability of interacting with the Writer window.
metadata.explanation: Task asks model to type a Chinese title into the empty docx. Custom getter reads docx text content, custom metric checks if the expected title appears in the document using exact match with fuzzy fallback.

scoring_breakdown.title_present: 1.0 - Expected title text found in document

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads docx file from VM and extracts all paragraph text using python-docx, returning structured data with text and paragraphs list.
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter directly as rules dict (expected.get('expected_title')) - proper handling per framework convention for type='rule'.
Postconfig correctly saves the document (Ctrl+S + Enter) before getter reads file content, ensuring state freshness.
Exact match check with fuzzy fallback (rapidfuzz partial_ratio >= 0.8) is a reasonable approach for Chinese text verification.

Minor coverage gap: instruction says 'at the top' but metric only checks if the title exists anywhere in the document, not that it is the first paragraph. For a mostly-empty document this is acceptable but not fully precise.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking that the title appears as the first paragraph (result['paragraphs'][0]) rather than anywhere in the full text, to verify the 'at the top' requirement more precisely.
